title: How the Internet Works
summary: How a message crosses the world in a fraction of a second: packets, cables and addresses.

steps.title: A network of networks
sentences: The internet is a huge network of connected computers all over the world.
Your phone connects to a nearby router, the router connects to your internet provider, and providers connect to each other.
Most of the world's internet traffic travels through cables, many of them under the sea.
points: Many cables are under the sea

steps.title: Addresses
sentences: Every device on the internet has an address, called an IP address.
We use easy names such as websites, and a system called DNS works like a phone book that turns the name into the address.
That way you can type a name instead of a number.

steps.title: Packets
sentences: When you send a photo, it is broken into many small pieces called packets.
Each packet travels by the best path it can find, and they may take different routes.
At the other end they are put back together in the right order.

steps.title: Staying safe
sentences: Not everything on the internet is true or safe.
Use strong passwords, do not share personal details with strangers and ask an adult if something feels wrong.
Check a fact in more than one reliable place before you believe it.

facts: The World Wide Web, the pages we browse, is only one part of the internet. Email and video calls use the internet too.
Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989.
Light signals inside glass fibre cables carry the data very fast.

quiz.q: What turns a website name into an address?
quiz.why: DNS is like the internet's phone book.

quiz.q: What are the small pieces of data called?
Where do many internet cables run?
quiz.why: Many cables are laid on the sea floor.
